- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) or shows strong negative drift.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >85) — model tends to overreact and peak too early.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: model often fails to correct for recent sharp declines (e.g., >75) and overcorrects on rebounds.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model typically peaks 1–2 days after true price turns.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.6 to 0.2), model fails to adjust downward quickly — underestimates downside risk.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days — especially when sentiment is weak or volatile.
